narrative.overview:
LifeGoods is a calm, evidence-forward shopping utility for Cambodian shoppers evaluating sealed packaged foods and beverages. Its central metaphor—Open Label—is represented by layered package-label sheets that reveal underlying label facts while keeping original source evidence in plain view. The design communicates clarity and rigor without adopting the promotional aesthetics of wellness marketing or clinical alarmism.

The visual atmosphere rests on a warm-white paper ground (#fafaf8), crisp charcoal black typography (#111111), rich palm sugar caramel interaction accents (#8a4b16), and golden palm sugar identity accents (#b86a1a) reserved for the Open Label mark and scanner action. Depth is established through tonal shifts and crisp one-pixel rules rather than decorative shadow cards. The entire experience is Khmer-first, pairing generous line heights with unclipped script rendering while keeping original package languages (Khmer, English, Vietnamese, Chinese, Thai) intact.
keyCharacteristics: Evidence Before Reassurance: Missing fields are explicitly Unavailable rather than assumed safe or absent; community data is clearly attributed.
Khmer-First Hierarchy: System sans typography tuned for complex Khmer ascenders and descenders with minimum 1.65 line heights.
Flat Paper Aesthetic: Clean warm-white background, pale functional containers, and crisp 1px borders without heavy skeuomorphic shadows or glassmorphism.

Strict Color Semantics: Palm sugar guides navigation and actions; golden palm sugar identifies brand and scan; crimson signals validation/error; green is never used to imply product health or purchase approval.

rules.name: The Color Neutrality Rule
rules.body: Color never communicates a health rating, safety verdict, allergen absence, or purchase recommendation. Green is never used as an endorsement.

rules.name: The Palm Sugar Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Golden Palm Sugar (#b86a1a) is strictly reserved for the Open Label brand mark and the primary Scan action. It is never used as an indicator of evidence severity or product status.

rules.name: The Khmer Line-Height Rule
rules.body: Khmer text requires a minimum line height of 1.65 for body and 1.7 for headings to avoid clipping subscript consonants and diacritics.

rules.name: The No-Truncation Rule
rules.body: Consequential product names, ingredient declarations, provenance notes, and uncertainty statements must wrap fully rather than truncate with ellipsis.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content containers, evidence panels, and search results rest flush against the page ground. Depth is communicated via 1px border rules and subtle surface fills rather than card drop shadows.

dos: Preserve field-level provenance, source attribution, and original language text alongside Khmer translations.
Explicitly mark missing or unreviewed data as 'Unavailable from Open Food Facts' rather than 'None'.
Keep touch targets at or above 44×44 CSS pixels across all viewports.
Test layouts with real multi-line Khmer script to ensure line heights and wrapping behave cleanly.
Provide immediate fallback to manual search on camera hesitation or permission refusal.
donts: Do not use green, traffic-light badges, or checkmarks to imply that a product is safe, healthy, or approved.
Do not use health scores, wellness purity marketing, or universal product ratings.
Do not collapse incomplete, missing, or contradictory evidence into a reassuring negative finding.
Do not apply heavy drop shadows, card stacking, glassmorphism, or gradient backgrounds.
Do not truncate product names, ingredients, or uncertainty disclosures.
